1	# Paper Framing — gen-depth-fingerprint
2	
3	## Target Venue
4	- **Primary: EMNLP 2026 ARR (deadline: May 25, 2026)** — D012
5	- Fallback: ICLR 2027 (Sep 24), NAACL 2027 ARR (Oct 16)
6	
7	## Core Insight
8	Non-paraphrastic LLM generation chains exhibit **differential depth response**: **central-tendency/diversity features** (entropy_mean, TTR, hapax ratio) drift monotonically with depth, while **distributional shape features** (entropy_std, tail_decay) remain near-stationary. This differential response is consistent with recursive generation inducing a **location shift** in the NLL distribution — the text becomes progressively more predictable (mean shifts) while the functional form of the distribution is preserved (shape is invariant). The genuine novelty is not the drift/stationarity split per se (which follows from location-shift properties), but: (a) the **task formulation** (ordinal depth estimation beyond binary detection), (b) **empirical validation** across 6 generators / 3 model families (including 7B+ scale) showing this pattern is robust, (c) the practical consequence that combining both feature types yields **complementary signal** for depth classification. **Primary metric (D017)**: binary LOGO F1 = 0.723 (gen-1 vs gen-2+, excluding gen-0 due to shared-seed leakage). 3-class LOGO F1 = 0.789 reported as supplementary with gen-0 caveat. Per-generator held-out F1: 0.68–0.86 (std=0.058). Key finding: in binary evaluation (no gen-0 leakage), 7-feature (0.723) > 4-baseline ensemble (0.712) — baseline advantage in 3-class was entirely from gen-0 classification. Depth signal is scale-invariant as a phenomenon, though cross-scale classifier transfer shows a moderate gap (8B held-out F1=0.69 vs ≤2.8B 0.76-0.85).
9	
10	## Core Claims (3 条，均可证伪)
11	
12	**Claim 1 — Depth Discriminability**: Distributional features computed under a held-out reference model can classify text generation depth with F1 significantly above chance, generalizing across unseen generators (leave-one-generator-out evaluation). Primary metric: binary LOGO F1 = 0.723 (gen-1 vs gen-2+, gen-0 excluded due to shared-seed overlap). 3-class (gen-0/gen-1/gen-2+) LOGO F1 = 0.789 supplementary with caveat.
13	
14	**Claim 2 — Differential Depth Response & Feature Complementarity**: Depth-dependent features exhibit differential response: central-tendency/diversity features (entropy_mean, TTR, hapax_ratio) drift monotonically with depth (consistent with location shift in NLL distribution), while shape features (entropy_std, tail_decay) remain near-stationary. In binary eval, 7-feature ensemble (0.723) outperforms 4-baseline detector ensemble (0.712) by +1.1pp and all individual detectors (+1.1–19.9pp). The 4-baseline advantage in 3-class (0.796 vs 0.789) is entirely from gen-0 classification. Ordinal-specific methods (CORAL 0.771, Frank-Hall 0.793) do not outperform XGBoost (0.789) — CI overlap at 3-class granularity.
15	
16	**Claim 3 — Downstream Utility (Negative Finding)**: Depth-aware data curation does NOT improve downstream CLM quality compared to random subsampling. At equal data count, size_matched (random control, ppl=2.367) outperforms depth01 (depth-stratified, 2.387) and binary_filtered (2.389). The primary determinant is data quantity, not depth composition (all 12K samples → ppl=2.335). Depth fingerprinting is an effective **diagnostic** tool for characterizing provenance, but not a **curative** tool for data curation. This honest negative finding is reported transparently.
17	
18	## Story Spine
19	
20	**Problem**: Web-scraped training data increasingly contains LLM-generated text of unknown provenance depth. Current detection methods offer only binary real-vs-synthetic classification, forcing all-or-nothing filtering: discard everything flagged as synthetic (losing useful gen-1 content) or keep everything (admitting high-risk deep-generation text with compounding distributional drift).
21	
22	**Existing approaches & gaps**: Binary detectors (FastDetectGPT, SynthID-Text, LD-Score) cannot distinguish gen-1 from gen-2+. Attractor cycle theory (ACL 2025) proves paraphrasing chains converge to 2-period cycles, bounding depth signal to ~3 classes — but this result depends on the semantic-preservation constraint of paraphrasing. No existing work attempts generation depth estimation. When repurposed as ordinal depth predictors, single detector scores (Avg-LogProb 0.737, LD-Score 0.655, FastDetectGPT 0.688, Binoculars 0.417 under 6-gen LOGO) show moderate signal but **high per-generator F1 variance** (e.g., AvgLogProb range 0.615–0.805, 19.0pp span), making them unreliable as standalone depth estimators.
23	
24	**Our framing**: We characterize distributional drift in recursive non-paraphrastic LLM generation, revealing **differential depth response**: level/diversity features (including reference-model entropy_mean) drift monotonically with depth, while distributional shape features (entropy variance, tail decay) remain near-stationary. This split is about **what the feature measures** (central tendency vs shape), not where it comes from. The combination of drifting and stationary features yields a 7-feature ensemble that **significantly and consistently** outperforms all single-detector baselines: binary LOGO F1 = 0.723 (gen-1 vs gen-2+, p<0.001 vs Avg-LogProb 0.712, LD-Score 0.701, FastDetectGPT 0.616, Binoculars 0.524). In the leak-free binary evaluation, 7-feature (0.723) > 4-baseline ensemble (0.712), reversing the 3-class result where baseline advantage came entirely from gen-0 classification. The practical advantage is **reliability across unknown generators** — per-generator F1 std = 0.058 for our ensemble vs higher variance for individual detectors.
25	
26	**Headline result template**: "On non-paraphrastic continuation chains across 6 base-model generators from 3 model families (0.6B–8.2B), our 7-feature distributional ensemble achieves binary LOGO F1 of 0.72 for leak-free depth discrimination (gen-1 vs gen-2+), outperforming all individual detection baselines. Per-generator held-out F1 ranges from 0.68 to 0.86 (std=0.051). Depth-aware data curation does not outperform random subsampling for downstream CLM quality, establishing depth fingerprinting as a diagnostic tool for provenance characterization, not a curative tool for data selection."
27	
28	## Anticipated Reviewer Concerns
29	
30	**RC1 — "Is this just vocabulary impoverishment?"**: Surface features alone achieve 0.73 macro-F1, but full 7-feature ensemble achieves 0.789 3-class / 0.723 binary (p<0.001). We don't claim reference features are "better" — we show they capture a **different, complementary** signal (stationary distributional shape vs drifting level/diversity). Note: "fingerprint" in the paper refers to the full feature vector's combination, not just reference-model features.
31	
32	**RC7 — Pre-registered prediction (LD-Score)**: LD-Score (character-distribution signature) measures character-level distributional properties. We predict it is a **level feature** (sensitive to vocabulary/character frequency shifts) and should exhibit **H₂ drift** with depth. This prediction is registered before plan_011 execution as an out-of-sample test of the level/shape framework.
33	
34	**RC2 — "Does this generalize beyond Pythia?"**: MVP used same-family models (Pythia-2.8B generator + Pythia-410M reference). → Cross-family experiments: Qwen/OLMo generators + non-Pythia reference models (RQ1 cross-generator evaluation).
35	
36	**RC3 — "Is 3-class sufficient? Why not finer-grained?"**: Attractor theory bounds paraphrasing to ~3 classes. → Secondary analysis: finer-grained ordinal classification (gen-0 through gen-4) on non-paraphrastic chains to test if more depth signal exists.
37	
38	**RC4 — "How realistic are single-model chains?"**: Real web contamination involves diverse generators. → Cross-model chains (different generator per depth step) as primary evaluation setting (RQ3).
39	
40	**RC5 — "What about human editing / post-processing?"**: Real-world synthetic text is often edited. → Robustness test with simulated human edits (random word replacement as lower-bound + LLM-simulated editing).
41	
42	**RC6 — "Ecological validity — continuation vs real web content"**: Lab-constructed chains may not match wild distribution. → Multi-domain seeds (news, Wikipedia, scientific, creative) + multiple prompt types (continuation, elaboration, inspired rewriting).
43	
44	**RC8 — "Aren't these just OOD detection features?"**: Reference-model entropy statistics are functionally NLL-based OOD scores (same signal backbone as DetectGPT/GLTR/Binoculars). Our contribution is NOT the features themselves but: (a) the problem formulation (ordinal depth estimation, not binary detection), (b) the empirical discovery that these features exhibit dual dynamics (level drift vs shape stationarity) under recursive generation, and (c) the practical application to risk-stratified data curation. Paper must explicitly connect to OOD detection + perplexity-based detection literature and position the contribution as primarily empirical/conceptual rather than methodological.
45	
46	**RC9 — "Only ≤2.8B generators — does this transfer to frontier scale?"**: **Answered (plan-014, D011).** Qwen3-8B (7.6B params) added as 6th generator. Depth signal IS present at 8B scale — all feature-depth Spearman correlations significant. Cross-scale transfer gap: 8B held-out F1=0.69 vs ≤2.8B 0.76-0.85. P0-B volume-matched control: adding Qwen3-8B's +1.1pp improvement is 94% from generator diversity, not data volume. **Paper framing**: depth signal universality supported; cross-scale gap is honest limitation; scope narrowed to base models (see N3/N4 fixes).
47	
48	**RC10 — "Text length confound"**: Hapax ratio and TTR are mechanically length-dependent. If generation chains produce texts of systematically different lengths, surface features may track length artifacts rather than distributional drift. → Length distribution analysis + length-normalized features + length-matched comparison (plan_013). Critical confound control.
49	
50	**RC11 — "Downstream utility — single run, no CIs"**: Depth-aware filtering advantage must be validated with multiple seeds + bootstrap CIs + sample-count-matched comparison (to control for data size confound). Must use non-Pythia model for downstream fine-tuning (OLMo-1B) to avoid reference model circularity (Pythia-410M as both feature extractor and eval model).
51	
52	## Contribution Positioning (D006+D007)
53	The contribution is **primarily empirical and conceptual**, not methodological:
54	1. **Problem formulation**: Ordinal depth estimation as a new task beyond binary detection (genuinely novel — no prior work)
55	2. **Empirical characterization**: Differential depth response across 6 generators / 3 families (including 7B+ scale), with robust cross-generator generalization (binary LOGO F1=0.723, 3-class LOGO F1=0.789). Scale-invariant phenomenon with honest cross-scale transfer gap.
56	3. **Negative finding**: Depth-aware data curation does NOT improve downstream CLM quality — depth fingerprinting is diagnostic, not curative (D009).
57	
58	**Framing discipline (D007 — re-dream consensus):**
59	- Do NOT call the drift/stationarity split a "discovery" — it follows from location-shift properties of the NLL distribution (means shift under distributional drift, shapes don't). Acknowledge this explicitly.
60	- Do NOT use H1/H2 terminology (overloads time-series unit-root convention). Use "drifting" vs "stationary" or "differential response."
61	- Do NOT overclaim "dual dynamics" as a novel theoretical framework. Use "differential depth response" — more calibrated.
62	- Consider renaming "distributional fingerprinting" → "distributional depth profiling" (fingerprinting implies source identification, creates confusion with LLM attribution literature).
63	- Provide at least a speculative theoretical motivation for WHY shape features remain stationary (e.g., "shape is determined by sampling mechanism and architecture, invariant to input content drift").
64	- Report **realistic performance range** (0.68–0.86 per-generator held-out F1, binary LOGO F1=0.72, 3-class LOGO F1=0.79 with gen-0 caveat) in abstract/conclusion, not just best-case. **禁止用 CI width 作为 cross-generator 一致性论据**（Round 2 C1 critical）——用 per-gen F1 std/range 替代。
65	- R² on 5 aggregated depth means is statistically meaningless (3 df). Use individual-level Spearman ρ with bootstrap CIs throughout.
66	
67	Related work must expand to 30+ references covering: perplexity-based detection (DetectGPT, GLTR, DNA-GPT, Binoculars), model collapse theory (Alemohammad et al., Dohmatob et al., Gerstgrasser et al., Guo et al.), OOD detection (Hendrycks & Gimpel), data quality scoring (DSIR, QuRating, CCNet), watermarking (Kirchenbauer et al.), vocabulary diversity (Guo et al. 2024, Padmakumar & He 2024, Holtzman et al. 2020), **stylometry/authorship attribution** (Stamatatos 2009, Koppel et al. 2009 — feature set is essentially stylometric), **iterative generation** (LLM as Broken Telephone ACL 2025, Markovian Generation Chains), **membership inference** (Shi et al. 2024).
68	
69	## Venue Fit
70	- **EMNLP 2026**: Excellent fit — directly addresses "New Missions for NLP Research" theme (data contamination, synthetic data feedback loops, data governance). NLP-native venue. Empirical/conceptual contributions well-received. Novel task formulation + honest negative finding valued.

# Paper Framing — gen-depth-fingerprint

## Target Venue
- **Primary: EMNLP 2026 ARR (deadline: May 25, 2026)** — D012
- Fallback: ICLR 2027 (Sep 24), NAACL 2027 ARR (Oct 16)

## Core Insight
Non-paraphrastic LLM generation chains exhibit **differential depth response**: **central-tendency/diversity features** (entropy_mean, TTR, hapax ratio) drift monotonically with depth, while **distributional shape features** (entropy_std, tail_decay) remain near-stationary. This differential response is consistent with recursive generation inducing a **location shift** in the NLL distribution — the text becomes progressively more predictable (mean shifts) while the functional form of the distribution is preserved (shape is invariant). The genuine novelty is not the drift/stationarity split per se (which follows from location-shift properties), but: (a) the **task formulation** (ordinal depth estimation beyond binary detection), (b) **empirical validation** across 6 generators / 3 model families (including 7B+ scale) showing this pattern is robust, (c) the practical consequence that combining both feature types yields **complementary signal** for depth classification. **Primary metric (D017)**: binary LOGO F1 = 0.723 (gen-1 vs gen-2+, excluding gen-0 due to shared-seed leakage). 3-class LOGO F1 = 0.789 reported as supplementary with gen-0 caveat. Per-generator held-out F1: 0.68–0.86 (std=0.058). Key finding: in binary evaluation (no gen-0 leakage), 7-feature (0.723) > 4-baseline ensemble (0.712) — baseline advantage in 3-class was entirely from gen-0 classification. Depth signal is scale-invariant as a phenomenon, though cross-scale classifier transfer shows a moderate gap (8B held-out F1=0.69 vs ≤2.8B 0.76-0.85).

## Core Claims (3 条，均可证伪)

**Claim 1 — Depth Discriminability**: Distributional features computed under a held-out reference model can classify text generation depth with F1 significantly above chance, generalizing across unseen generators (leave-one-generator-out evaluation). Primary metric: binary LOGO F1 = 0.723 (gen-1 vs gen-2+, gen-0 excluded due to shared-seed overlap). 3-class (gen-0/gen-1/gen-2+) LOGO F1 = 0.789 supplementary with caveat.

**Claim 2 — Differential Depth Response & Feature Complementarity**: Depth-dependent features exhibit differential response: central-tendency/diversity features (entropy_mean, TTR, hapax_ratio) drift monotonically with depth (consistent with location shift in NLL distribution), while shape features (entropy_std, tail_decay) remain near-stationary. In binary eval, 7-feature ensemble (0.723) outperforms 4-baseline detector ensemble (0.712) by +1.1pp and all individual detectors (+1.1–19.9pp). The 4-baseline advantage in 3-class (0.796 vs 0.789) is entirely from gen-0 classification. Ordinal-specific methods (CORAL 0.771, Frank-Hall 0.793) do not outperform XGBoost (0.789) — CI overlap at 3-class granularity.

**Claim 3 — Downstream Utility (Negative Finding)**: Depth-aware data curation does NOT improve downstream CLM quality compared to random subsampling. At equal data count, size_matched (random control, ppl=2.367) outperforms depth01 (depth-stratified, 2.387) and binary_filtered (2.389). The primary determinant is data quantity, not depth composition (all 12K samples → ppl=2.335). Depth fingerprinting is an effective **diagnostic** tool for characterizing provenance, but not a **curative** tool for data curation. This honest negative finding is reported transparently.

## Story Spine

**Problem**: Web-scraped training data increasingly contains LLM-generated text of unknown provenance depth. Current detection methods offer only binary real-vs-synthetic classification, forcing all-or-nothing filtering: discard everything flagged as synthetic (losing useful gen-1 content) or keep everything (admitting high-risk deep-generation text with compounding distributional drift).

**Existing approaches & gaps**: Binary detectors (FastDetectGPT, SynthID-Text, LD-Score) cannot distinguish gen-1 from gen-2+. Attractor cycle theory (ACL 2025) proves paraphrasing chains converge to 2-period cycles, bounding depth signal to ~3 classes — but this result depends on the semantic-preservation constraint of paraphrasing. No existing work attempts generation depth estimation. When repurposed as ordinal depth predictors, single detector scores (Avg-LogProb 0.737, LD-Score 0.655, FastDetectGPT 0.688, Binoculars 0.417 under 6-gen LOGO) show moderate signal but **high per-generator F1 variance** (e.g., AvgLogProb range 0.615–0.805, 19.0pp span), making them unreliable as standalone depth estimators.

**Our framing**: We characterize distributional drift in recursive non-paraphrastic LLM generation, revealing **differential depth response**: level/diversity features (including reference-model entropy_mean) drift monotonically with depth, while distributional shape features (entropy variance, tail decay) remain near-stationary. This split is about **what the feature measures** (central tendency vs shape), not where it comes from. The combination of drifting and stationary features yields a 7-feature ensemble that **significantly and consistently** outperforms all single-detector baselines: binary LOGO F1 = 0.723 (gen-1 vs gen-2+, p<0.001 vs Avg-LogProb 0.712, LD-Score 0.701, FastDetectGPT 0.616, Binoculars 0.524). In the leak-free binary evaluation, 7-feature (0.723) > 4-baseline ensemble (0.712), reversing the 3-class result where baseline advantage came entirely from gen-0 classification. The practical advantage is **reliability across unknown generators** — per-generator F1 std = 0.058 for our ensemble vs higher variance for individual detectors.

**Headline result template**: "On non-paraphrastic continuation chains across 6 base-model generators from 3 model families (0.6B–8.2B), our 7-feature distributional ensemble achieves binary LOGO F1 of 0.72 for leak-free depth discrimination (gen-1 vs gen-2+), outperforming all individual detection baselines. Per-generator held-out F1 ranges from 0.68 to 0.86 (std=0.051). Depth-aware data curation does not outperform random subsampling for downstream CLM quality, establishing depth fingerprinting as a diagnostic tool for provenance characterization, not a curative tool for data selection."

## Anticipated Reviewer Concerns

**RC1 — "Is this just vocabulary impoverishment?"**: Surface features alone achieve 0.73 macro-F1, but full 7-feature ensemble achieves 0.789 3-class / 0.723 binary (p<0.001). We don't claim reference features are "better" — we show they capture a **different, complementary** signal (stationary distributional shape vs drifting level/diversity). Note: "fingerprint" in the paper refers to the full feature vector's combination, not just reference-model features.

**RC7 — Pre-registered prediction (LD-Score)**: LD-Score (character-distribution signature) measures character-level distributional properties. We predict it is a **level feature** (sensitive to vocabulary/character frequency shifts) and should exhibit **H₂ drift** with depth. This prediction is registered before plan_011 execution as an out-of-sample test of the level/shape framework.

**RC2 — "Does this generalize beyond Pythia?"**: MVP used same-family models (Pythia-2.8B generator + Pythia-410M reference). → Cross-family experiments: Qwen/OLMo generators + non-Pythia reference models (RQ1 cross-generator evaluation).

**RC3 — "Is 3-class sufficient? Why not finer-grained?"**: Attractor theory bounds paraphrasing to ~3 classes. → Secondary analysis: finer-grained ordinal classification (gen-0 through gen-4) on non-paraphrastic chains to test if more depth signal exists.

**RC4 — "How realistic are single-model chains?"**: Real web contamination involves diverse generators. → Cross-model chains (different generator per depth step) as primary evaluation setting (RQ3).

**RC5 — "What about human editing / post-processing?"**: Real-world synthetic text is often edited. → Robustness test with simulated human edits (random word replacement as lower-bound + LLM-simulated editing).

**RC6 — "Ecological validity — continuation vs real web content"**: Lab-constructed chains may not match wild distribution. → Multi-domain seeds (news, Wikipedia, scientific, creative) + multiple prompt types (continuation, elaboration, inspired rewriting).

**RC8 — "Aren't these just OOD detection features?"**: Reference-model entropy statistics are functionally NLL-based OOD scores (same signal backbone as DetectGPT/GLTR/Binoculars). Our contribution is NOT the features themselves but: (a) the problem formulation (ordinal depth estimation, not binary detection), (b) the empirical discovery that these features exhibit dual dynamics (level drift vs shape stationarity) under recursive generation, and (c) the practical application to risk-stratified data curation. Paper must explicitly connect to OOD detection + perplexity-based detection literature and position the contribution as primarily empirical/conceptual rather than methodological.

**RC9 — "Only ≤2.8B generators — does this transfer to frontier scale?"**: **Answered (plan-014, D011).** Qwen3-8B (7.6B params) added as 6th generator. Depth signal IS present at 8B scale — all feature-depth Spearman correlations significant. Cross-scale transfer gap: 8B held-out F1=0.69 vs ≤2.8B 0.76-0.85. P0-B volume-matched control: adding Qwen3-8B's +1.1pp improvement is 94% from generator diversity, not data volume. **Paper framing**: depth signal universality supported; cross-scale gap is honest limitation; scope narrowed to base models (see N3/N4 fixes).

**RC10 — "Text length confound"**: Hapax ratio and TTR are mechanically length-dependent. If generation chains produce texts of systematically different lengths, surface features may track length artifacts rather than distributional drift. → Length distribution analysis + length-normalized features + length-matched comparison (plan_013). Critical confound control.

**RC11 — "Downstream utility — single run, no CIs"**: Depth-aware filtering advantage must be validated with multiple seeds + bootstrap CIs + sample-count-matched comparison (to control for data size confound). Must use non-Pythia model for downstream fine-tuning (OLMo-1B) to avoid reference model circularity (Pythia-410M as both feature extractor and eval model).

## Contribution Positioning (D006+D007)
The contribution is **primarily empirical and conceptual**, not methodological:
1. **Problem formulation**: Ordinal depth estimation as a new task beyond binary detection (genuinely novel — no prior work)
2. **Empirical characterization**: Differential depth response across 6 generators / 3 families (including 7B+ scale), with robust cross-generator generalization (binary LOGO F1=0.723, 3-class LOGO F1=0.789). Scale-invariant phenomenon with honest cross-scale transfer gap.
3. **Negative finding**: Depth-aware data curation does NOT improve downstream CLM quality — depth fingerprinting is diagnostic, not curative (D009).

**Framing discipline (D007 — re-dream consensus):**
- Do NOT call the drift/stationarity split a "discovery" — it follows from location-shift properties of the NLL distribution (means shift under distributional drift, shapes don't). Acknowledge this explicitly.
- Do NOT use H1/H2 terminology (overloads time-series unit-root convention). Use "drifting" vs "stationary" or "differential response."
- Do NOT overclaim "dual dynamics" as a novel theoretical framework. Use "differential depth response" — more calibrated.
- Consider renaming "distributional fingerprinting" → "distributional depth profiling" (fingerprinting implies source identification, creates confusion with LLM attribution literature).
- Provide at least a speculative theoretical motivation for WHY shape features remain stationary (e.g., "shape is determined by sampling mechanism and architecture, invariant to input content drift").
- Report **realistic performance range** (0.68–0.86 per-generator held-out F1, binary LOGO F1=0.72, 3-class LOGO F1=0.79 with gen-0 caveat) in abstract/conclusion, not just best-case. **禁止用 CI width 作为 cross-generator 一致性论据**（Round 2 C1 critical）——用 per-gen F1 std/range 替代。
- R² on 5 aggregated depth means is statistically meaningless (3 df). Use individual-level Spearman ρ with bootstrap CIs throughout.

Related work must expand to 30+ references covering: perplexity-based detection (DetectGPT, GLTR, DNA-GPT, Binoculars), model collapse theory (Alemohammad et al., Dohmatob et al., Gerstgrasser et al., Guo et al.), OOD detection (Hendrycks & Gimpel), data quality scoring (DSIR, QuRating, CCNet), watermarking (Kirchenbauer et al.), vocabulary diversity (Guo et al. 2024, Padmakumar & He 2024, Holtzman et al. 2020), **stylometry/authorship attribution** (Stamatatos 2009, Koppel et al. 2009 — feature set is essentially stylometric), **iterative generation** (LLM as Broken Telephone ACL 2025, Markovian Generation Chains), **membership inference** (Shi et al. 2024).

## Venue Fit
- **EMNLP 2026**: Excellent fit — directly addresses "New Missions for NLP Research" theme (data contamination, synthetic data feedback loops, data governance). NLP-native venue. Empirical/conceptual contributions well-received. Novel task formulation + honest negative finding valued.

## Open Questions (pending P1-C)
- Instruct model depth response: if Qwen3-1.7B-Instruct shows drift → extend to 1-2 more instruct models; if not → limitation paragraph (scope narrowing already in place)
- Rd2-W4 (no validated alternative application): diagnostic framing is current defense; no new experiment planned unless P1-C opens a new angle

The gen-2/gen-3 confusion rate of 0.45 across all methods suggests a fundamental limit: per-step distributional drift diminishes geometrically, and individual sample noise exceeds systematic depth differences after 2 generations.
This is consistent with attractor convergence predictions, though our non-paraphrastic chains are not strictly bound by these theoretical results.

\paragraph{Diagnostic, not curative.}
The combination of strong depth discriminability (LOGO F1=0.78) with null downstream utility establishes a clear positioning: depth profiling characterizes provenance (``how recursive is this corpus?'') but cannot improve data selection.
The primary determinant of downstream quality is data quantity, not depth composition.

%==============================================================================
\section{Conclusion}

We present the first systematic empirical study of generation depth estimation in recursive LLM output.
Our 7-feature distributional ensemble achieves 3-class LOGO F1 of 0.78 across 5 generators from 3 model families, with per-generator held-out F1 ranging from 0.73 to 0.84.
We identify differential depth response---diversity features drift while shape features remain stationary---and demonstrate that this pattern enables cross-architecture depth classification.

Key limitations include: (1) the architecture-dependent transfer gap, with OLMo showing 11pp lower performance than same-family Pythia; (2) a $\sim$3-class resolution ceiling, with finer-grained classification degrading to F1=0.49; (3) null downstream utility, limiting the practical contribution to diagnostic provenance characterization.
